Let’s use this formula to derive the volumes of a cone and sphere:

spec.description: Triangular generating region from (0,r) to (h,0), circular slice and dashed lower cone silhouette/base. Curved arrow indicates revolution about the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: y=r(1-x/h), 0≤x≤h; rotation produces a cone of radius r and height h. Display coordinates are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: permanent supplied diagram

answer.worked:
The line through $(0,r)$ and $(h,0)$ is $y=r-\dfrac rhx$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_0^h\left(r-\frac rhx\right)^2\,dx\\&=\pi r^2\int_0^h\left(1-\frac{2x}{h}+\frac{x^2}{h^2}\right)\,dx\\&=\pi r^2\left[x-\frac{x^2}{h}+\frac{x^3}{3h^2}\right]_0^h\\&=\pi r^2\left(h-h+\frac h3\right)\\&=\frac13\pi r^2h\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Upper semicircle shaded blue with labelled intercepts and top point; dashed lower semicircle and central perspective outline, a thin circular slice to the right of the y-axis and rotation arrow.
spec.mathematics: x²+y²=r², y≥0, −r≤x≤r; revolution about the x-axis generates a sphere of radius r.
spec.answerVisibility: permanent supplied diagram

answer.worked:
The semicircle satisfies $x^2+y^2=r^2$, so $y^2=r^2-x^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_{-r}^{r}(r^2-x^2)\,dx\\&=\pi\left[r^2x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-r}^{r}\\&=\pi\left[\left(r^3-\frac{r^3}{3}\right)-\left(-r^3+\frac{r^3}{3}\right)\right]\\&=\frac43\pi r^3\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
At the intersections,
$$\begin{aligned}x^2&=x+2\\x^2-x-2&=0\\(x-2)(x+1)&=0\\x&=-1\text{ or }2.\end{aligned}$$
The line is above the parabola between the intersections.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-1}^{2}(x+2-x^2)\,dx\\A&=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}+2x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-1}^{2}\\A&=\frac{10}{3}-\left(-\frac76\right)\\A&=\frac92\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
Outer radius $=x+2$, inner radius $=x^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_{-1}^{2}\left((x+2)^2-x^4\right)\,dx\\V&=\pi\int_{-1}^{2}(x^2+4x+4-x^4)\,dx\\V&=\pi\left[\frac{x^3}{3}+2x^2+4x-\frac{x^5}{5}\right]_{-1}^{2}\\V&=\pi\left(\frac{184}{15}-\left(-\frac{32}{15}\right)\right)\\V&=\frac{72\pi}{5}\text{ units}^3.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
The curves meet where $x^2=\dfrac8x$, so $x^3=8$ and $x=2$.
For $1\le x\le2$ the hyperbola is above the parabola.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_1^2\left(\frac8x-x^2\right)\,dx\\&=\left[8\ln x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_1^2\\&=\left(8\ln2-\frac83\right)-\left(0-\frac13\right)\\&=8\ln2-\frac73\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
The curves meet where $e^x=6-e^x$, so $e^x=3$ and $x=\ln3$.
For $0\le x\le\ln3$ the curve $y=6-e^x$ is above $y=e^x$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_0^{\ln3}(6-2e^x)\,dx\\&=\left[6x-2e^x\right]_0^{\ln3}\\&=(6\ln3-6)-(0-2)\\&=6\ln3-4\text{ u}^2.\end{aligned}$$

&= \pi\left(r^3-\frac{r^3}{3}-r^2(r-w)+\frac{(r-w)^3}{3}\right) \\
&= \pi\left(rw^2-\frac{w^3}{3}\right) \\
&= \frac{\pi}{3}(3r-w)w^2
\end{align*}$$

Rearrange for $x$:

For $\frac{\pi}{2}\le y<\frac{3\pi}{2}$ the area lies to the right of the $y$-axis ($x>0$); for $\frac{3\pi}{2}<y\le\frac{5\pi}{2}$ it lies to the left ($x<0$). Each horizontal cross-section is a disc of radius $|x|$ with area $\pi x^2$, and $x^2=4\cos^2\left(\frac y3\right)$ is valid on both sides of the neck.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{5\pi}{2}}x^2\,dy\\&=4\pi\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{5\pi}{2}}\cos^2\left(\frac y3\right)dy\\&=2\pi\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{5\pi}{2}}\left(1+\cos\frac{2y}{3}\right)dy\\&=2\pi\left[y+\frac32\sin\frac{2y}{3}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{5\pi}{2}}\\&=2\pi\left[2\pi+\frac32\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}-\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]\\&=2\pi\left(2\pi-\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\&=4\pi^2-3\sqrt3\,\pi\text{ units}^3.\end{aligned}$$

content.prompt:
Below is the graph of the function $y=3\cos^{-1}x$.
Find the exact volume of the solid of revolution formed if the area bounded by $y=3\cos^{-1}x$, the coordinate axes and the line $x=-1$ is rotated about the $y$-axis.

answer.short:

Subtract the volume removed from the full cylinder of radius $1$ and height $3\pi$.
answer.worked:
Rearrange the curve in terms of $y$:
$$\begin{align*}
y&=3\cos^{-1}x\\
x&=\cos\left(\frac{y}{3}\right)
\end{align*}$$
The full cylinder has radius $1$ and height $3\pi$:
$$\begin{align*}
V_c&=\pi(1)^2(3\pi)\\
&=3\pi^2
\end{align*}$$
The volume removed is:
$$\begin{align*}
V_1&=\pi\int_{\frac{3\pi}{2}}^{3\pi}\cos^2\left(\frac{y}{3}\right)\,dy\\
&=\frac{\pi}{2}\int_{\frac{3\pi}{2}}^{3\pi}\left(1+\cos\left(\frac{2y}{3}\right)\right)\,dy\\
&=\frac{\pi}{2}\left[y+\frac{3}{2}\sin\left(\frac{2y}{3}\right)\right]_{\frac{3\pi}{2}}^{3\pi}\\
&=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(3\pi-\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{3\pi^2}{4}
\end{align*}$$
Therefore:
$$\begin{align*}
V&=V_c-V_1\\
&=3\pi^2-\frac{3\pi^2}{4}\\
&=\frac{9\pi^2}{4}
\end{align*}$$
The volume is $\frac{9\pi^2}{4}\text{ units}^3$.

Show that the volume of wine in the glass is given by:
$$V=\frac{\pi}{4}(9\pi-6u+8\cos u+\sin 2u).$$

answer.worked:
The cavity ends at $x=\frac{3\pi}{2}$ (the support is excluded), so the wine occupies $u\le x\le\frac{3\pi}{2}$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\int_u^{\frac{3\pi}{2}}(1+\sin x)^2\,dx\\&=\pi\int_u^{\frac{3\pi}{2}}\left(1+2\sin x+\frac{1-\cos 2x}{2}\right)dx\\&=\pi\int_u^{\frac{3\pi}{2}}\left(\frac32+2\sin x-\frac12\cos 2x\right)dx\\&=\pi\left[\frac{3x}{2}-2\cos x-\frac14\sin 2x\right]_u^{\frac{3\pi}{2}}\\&=\pi\left[\frac{9\pi}{4}-\left(\frac{3u}{2}-2\cos u-\frac14\sin 2u\right)\right]\\&=\frac{\pi}{4}\left(9\pi-6u+8\cos u+\sin 2u\right).\end{aligned}$$

children.prompt: If wine is poured into the glass at a constant rate of $0.5\text{ cm}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$, at what rate will the depth of wine be increasing when the depth is $\frac{\pi}{2}\text{ cm}$?

answer.worked:
With the glass upright, the lowest interior point is $x=\frac{3\pi}{2}$, so the depth is $h=\frac{3\pi}{2}-u$ (not $u$). The level coordinate $u$ decreases as wine is added.

When $h=\frac{\pi}{2}$: $u=\frac{3\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{2}=\pi$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dV}{du}&=\frac{\pi}{4}\left(-6-8\sin u+2\cos 2u\right)\\\left.\frac{dV}{du}\right|_{u=\pi}&=\frac{\pi}{4}(-6-0+2)\\&=-\pi.\end{aligned}$$
(Check: $\frac{dV}{du}=-\pi(1+\sin u)^2=-\pi$ at $u=\pi$.)
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dV}{dt}&=\frac{dV}{du}\cdot\frac{du}{dt}\\0.5&=-\pi\frac{du}{dt}\\\frac{du}{dt}&=-\frac{1}{2\pi}.\end{aligned}$$
Since $h=\frac{3\pi}{2}-u$,
$$\frac{dh}{dt}=-\frac{du}{dt}=\frac{1}{2\pi}.$$
The depth is increasing at $\frac{1}{2\pi}\text{ cm/s}$.

answer.worked:
Make $x^2$ the subject of the equation of the curve:
$$\begin{align*}y&=9-\frac{9}{x^2}\\\frac{9}{x^2}&=9-y\\x^2&=\frac{9}{9-y}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi\int_0^h x^2\,dy\\&=\pi\int_0^h\frac{9}{9-y}\,dy\end{align*}$$
Differentiating with respect to $h$:
$$\frac{dV}{dh}=\frac{9\pi}{9-h}$$
Using $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{dV}{dh}\times\dfrac{dh}{dt}$ with $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=50$ and $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=\dfrac{50}{3\pi}$:
$$\begin{align*}50&=\frac{9\pi}{9-h}\times\frac{50}{3\pi}\\1&=\frac{3}{9-h}\\9-h&=3\\h&=6\end{align*}$$
The depth of the water is $6\text{ cm}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Determine the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $a$ and $b$.

answer.worked:
The roots are $\alpha,\alpha,\beta$ and the leading coefficient is $-1$, so $f(x)=-(x-\alpha)^2(x-\beta)$. Comparing coefficients with $-x^3+ax^2-20x+b$:
$$\begin{aligned}a&=2\alpha+\beta\\20&=\alpha^2+2\alpha\beta\\b&=\alpha^2\beta.\end{aligned}$$
With $\beta=2\alpha$:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+2\alpha(2\alpha)&=20\\5\alpha^2&=20\\\alpha^2&=4\\\alpha&=2\quad(\alpha>0).\end{aligned}$$
Hence $\beta=4$, $a=2(2)+4=8$ and $b=2^2\cdot4=16$.

Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\pi\left(\frac{91}{6}-4\sqrt3+\frac{169}{105}\right)\\&=\pi\left(\frac{3523}{210}-4\sqrt3\right).\end{aligned}$$
